academic_abramowitz.attribution: Our implementation of Abramowitz's published 2026 midterm equations, run on our generic-ballot average.

diagnostics.fit: OLS, 20 midterms 1946-2022; House R-squared > 0.8, Senate about 0.67

academic_referendum.name: Referendum (approval + income, no exposure)

inputs.approval_source: mean of 7 adults-sample approval poll(s) in the 14 days to 2026-10-24. Gallup interviewed adults, and so does this average; the residual house effect between Gallup and the rest of the adults field is under two points and cannot be re-measured now that Gallup has stopped polling, so it is left in the error bar rather than corrected for (Silver Bulletin poll list, aggregate only)
inputs.income_source: FRED income_growth_ytd as of 2026-10-24, 8 month(s) of the year in hand

academic_economic_pessimism.attribution: Our implementation of Lockerbie's published House equation. The open-seat term's SIGN is our assumption, not his — see the sensitivity table.

The model was fit on 1952-2022 and this is a linear extrapolation beyond anything in that sample, which is most of why it is the most Democratic forecast on this site.
